codebase.title: tmm: transfer-matrix optics for multilayer thin films
codebase.fingerprint_algorithm: SHA-256 over typed sorted regular-file paths+bytes and symlink paths+safe targets

agent_authored.description: tmm (Steven J. Byrnes, MIT) simulates a plane wave of one vacuum wavelength, angle of incidence and polarisation propagating through a planar stack of homogeneous layers, each with a complex refractive index and a thickness, between two semi-infinite media, by the transfer-matrix method of the Fresnel equations (arXiv:1603.02720). coh_tmm returns the complex reflection and transmission amplitudes, the reflected and transmitted power fractions, the power entering the stack and the forward and backward amplitudes in every layer; ellips, unpolarized_RT, position_resolved (Poynting vector, absorbed power density, E field at any depth), absorp_in_each_layer and absorp_analytic_fn derive the observables of ellipsometry and photovoltaic absorption modelling; inc_tmm handles thick incoherent layers around coherent sub-stacks by intensity transfer; color.py turns a reflectance spectrum into a CIE colour under an illuminant (needs colorpy). 1,912 lines of pure Python on NumPy; every call handles one wavelength and one angle, so spectra, angle scans and design sweeps are Python loops around it.
evidence: README.rst, __init__.py docstring and the docstrings of tmm_core.py at the pin

commands: python3.12 -m venv venv-tmm && venv-tmm/bin/pip install numpy scipy matplotlib   # numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, matplotlib 3.11.2 on Python 3.12.3
SRC=<scratch copy of the checkout, directory named tmm>
python -m pip install --no-deps --target $SITE $SRC   # SRC = the scratch copy of the checkout, SITE = an empty target directory; 3.8 s wall, build isolation on
PKG=<a directory holding a symlink named tmm to the checkout>   # the alternative: the checkout itself as the package directory on PYTHONPATH; identical test output
pitfalls: pip install --no-build-isolation fails in a bare Python 3.12 venv with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'setuptools' (venv no longer seeds setuptools); use the default build isolation or pip install setuptools first

the package is flat: pyproject.toml maps package 'tmm' to '.', so the checkout directory must be named tmm (or symlinked as such) to be importable without installing; the vendored tree under code/tmm/ has the right name by construction

landscape.how_to_run: python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.run_all()"   (no pytest, no assertions: each test prints difference fractions that should be zero within rounding)
landscape.notes: basic_test and position_resolved_test embed reference values from the author's earlier Mathematica program; the other six compare against physical identities (energy conservation, Poynting continuity, R+T=1, analytic vs numeric absorption, coherent vs incoherent averaging, overflow protection). Exit status is 0 whatever the numbers.

landscape.how_to_run: python -c "import tmm.examples as ex; ex.sample1()"  (each sample builds a Matplotlib figure and calls plt.show(); sample5 also prints rgb and xyY)
landscape.notes: sample3 reproduces Handbook of Ellipsometry (Tompkins 2005) Fig. 1.14, sample6 reproduces Mater. Trans. 51 (2010) 1150 Fig. 6a, sample5 compares against a published SiO2-on-Si colour chart; no numbers ship. sample5 needs colorpy.

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$SITE MPLBACKEND=Agg python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.run_all()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (basic_test and position_resolved_test against the embedded Mathematica values, largest difference fraction 1.0e-15; the identities hold to 1e-16)
outputs: stdout: 89 text lines of difference fractions and printed arrays
runs.nondeterminism: none seen: stdout byte-identical across two runs, and identical between the pip-installed package and the checkout on PYTHONPATH
pitfalls: nothing asserts and the exit status is always 0: a check must recompute the graded quantities itself, never parse pass/fail
the opacity warning is printed once per process through a module global, so stdout depends on which tests ran earlier in the same process; grade numbers, never the text

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.basic_test()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (r, t, R, T for s and p, psi and Delta against Mathematica; largest difference fraction 1.0e-15 on t_s, Delta 6.5e-14 because Delta itself is 2.1e-3)

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.position_resolved_test()"
runs.reproduced: yes: 15 digits (kz, Poynting vector and absorption at one depth against Mathematica, 2e-16 to 4e-16); absorption sums to 1 exactly; Poynting continuity and end-point identities at 1e-16; the finite-difference derivative check lands at 4.6e-12 (p) and 3.9e-11 (s), the O(h) stencil error, not a fault

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.position_resolved_test2()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): absorption sums to 1 exactly with complex incident and final media; continuity and end-point identities at 1e-16; finite difference at 5e-11

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.absorp_analytic_fn_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): the analytic absorption function equals position_resolved to 0 and 1.7e-16, and its flipped copy agrees from the other side

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.incoherent_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): inc_tmm against the closed-form three-layer sums and against coh_tmm at 1e-16 or exactly 0; the thickness-averaged (357 thicknesses) and wavelength-averaged (234 wavelengths) coherent runs agree with the incoherent result to 1.5e-5 to 8e-5, the finite-sample residual of the averaging, printed as 'discrepancy'
outputs: stdout: 14 difference fractions, 4 discrepancy lines, two 2x4 arrays
pitfalls: the 'discrepancy' lines are 1e-5 by design (finite averaging), not failures; a check grades the computed values, not their closeness to zero

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.RT_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identities only): R+T=1 at a single interface to 4.4e-16, power_entering equals T to 3.5e-16

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.coh_overflow_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identity only): the vw_list of the five-layer stack with a layer of imag(delta)=18850 agrees with the truncated three-layer stack in its first entries (printed, compared by eye: 0.6066665-0.1116073j both)
outputs: stdout: the opacity warning once, two printed complex arrays
pitfalls: imag(delta) > 35 is clamped to 35 in coh_tmm and a warning is printed once per process; amplitudes behind the opaque layer come out at 1e-16 to 1e-32, so a pointwise bound on vw_list needs an absolute term

runs.command: PYTHONPATH=$PKG python -c "import tmm.tests as t; t.inc_overflow_test()"
runs.reproduced: no reference (identity only): power_entering_list of the five-layer stack agrees with the three-layer stack in its first entries (0.4210526315789473 both)
outputs: stdout: two printed lists; under numpy 2 the entries print as np.float64(...)
pitfalls: single-pass transmission P < 1e-30 is floored to 1e-30 in inc_tmm, which sets the 1.97e-30 entries behind the opaque layer; the printed list format depends on the numpy major version, so grade numbers, not text

modules.title: tmm: transfer-matrix optics for multilayer thin films
entrypoints: tmm_core.coh_tmm(pol, n_list, d_list, th_0, lam_vac): the coherent transfer-matrix solve of one stack at one wavelength and angle (r, t, R, T, power_entering, vw_list, kz_list, th_list)
tmm_core.inc_tmm(pol, n_list, d_list, c_list, th_0, lam_vac): the incoherent or mixed coherent/incoherent solve (R, T, VW_list, power_entering_list, the coherent sub-stack results)
tmm_core.ellips, unpolarized_RT, position_resolved, absorp_in_each_layer, absorp_analytic_fn, inc_absorp_in_each_layer, inc_find_absorp_analytic_fn: the derived observables
color.calc_reflectances and calc_spectrum and calc_color: film colour under an illuminant (needs colorpy)
tests.run_all(): the eight official tests; examples.sample1..sample6: the six official examples
modules.expensive_path: Every solver call handles one wavelength, one angle and one polarisation with Python-level 2x2 complex matrix products and Fresnel coefficients per interface (coh_tmm: two loops over layers, then a backward sweep for vw_list; inc_tmm: two coh_tmm calls per coherent sub-stack plus the intensity transfer). Spectra, angle scans, thickness scans and every inverse-design loop are pure Python loops around it: sample5 alone makes 38,151 coh_tmm calls (8.4 s), sample1 1,200. What a port accelerates is the batched evaluation of many stacks, wavelengths and angles (the tmm_fast re-implementation reports about 100x from vectorisation and GPU execution).
modules.rationale: One package of 1,912 Python lines, one build (pip), one test file, one example file, one namespace; coh_tmm, inc_tmm, the derived observables and the colour layer share the same state (n_list, d_list, angles, the 2x2 matrices) and inc_tmm is built on coh_tmm, so no sub-part could carry its own task without the solver redesigning a sibling. The whole codebase is the module, slug tmm.
excluded: examples.ipynb: the six samples of examples.py pasted into notebook cells; deduplicated to the .py, which exercises every code path the notebook holds
manual.pdf and manual_source/manual.lyx: documentation, nothing runs
hazards: color.py and examples.sample5 need colorpy; the PyPI colorpy 0.1.1 is Python 2 only (import colormodels fails on Python 3); the fish2000/ColorPy fork (LGPL-3.0) at commit 4c9e5b2e334851b42626f9a1eda31197739b097e imports and runs on 3.12, so the colour check adds an LGPL third-party dependency to the images (installed, never vendored)

is_forward_angle decides the forward wave by a floating-point comparison with a 100*EPSILON threshold, and snell and list_snell flip the angle on it; coh_tmm clamps imag(delta) > 35 and inc_tmm floors P < 1e-30: discrete choices on floating-point values, far from the thresholds in every official deck
coh_tmm prints an opacity warning once per process through a module global; stdout is therefore process-history dependent and is never a graded observable
examples end in matplotlib.pyplot.show() (headless runs need MPLBACKEND=Agg or a stub) and colorpy.plots writes temp_plot.png into the working directory
sample2 depends on scipy.interpolate.interp1d(kind='quadratic') on complex data, a legacy SciPy interface
modules.purpose: Simulate reflection, transmission, absorption and ellipsometric response of planar multilayer thin and thick films by the transfer-matrix method; the whole package is the module.
primary_inputs: pol ('s' or 'p'), n_list (complex refractive index per layer, semi-infinite media first and last), d_list (thicknesses, inf at both ends), th_0 (angle of incidence, complex when the incident medium absorbs), lam_vac (vacuum wavelength); c_list (coherency per layer, 'c' or 'i') for inc_tmm
for position_resolved: a layer index and a depth into it; for color: index functions of wavelength and an illuminant table
primary_outputs: coh_tmm: r, t, R, T, power_entering, vw_list (forward/backward amplitudes per layer), kz_list, th_list
inc_tmm: R, T, VW_list (intensities per incoherent layer), power_entering_list, the coherent sub-stack results in both directions

ellips: psi, Delta; position_resolved: poyn, absor, Ex, Ey, Ez; absorp_in_each_layer and inc_absorp_in_each_layer: absorbed fraction per layer; absorp_analytic_fn: the four-exponential absorption profile coefficients; color: reflectance spectrum, XYZ, xyY, rgb, irgb
algorithm_stages: propagation angles per layer by Snell's law on the complex plane (list_snell, is_forward_angle picks the forward branch)
Fresnel amplitude coefficients per interface (interface_r, interface_t) and the per-layer phase delta = kz d (clamped at imag 35 for opaque layers)
2x2 characteristic matrices multiplied front to back (Mtilde) for r and t, then a backward sweep for the per-layer amplitudes vw_list
power fractions from the amplitudes (R_from_r, T_from_t, power_entering_from_r) and the depth-resolved Poynting vector, absorption and field
incoherent stacks: coh_tmm on each coherent sub-stack in both directions, then intensity transfer matrices across incoherent layers (inc_tmm), with per-layer absorption bookkeeping
colour: reflectance over 360-830 nm, product with the illuminant, CIE XYZ integration and sRGB conversion through colorpy
unique_responsibilities: the one-wavelength one-angle transfer-matrix solve of a planar multilayer and every observable derived from it
not_responsible_for: examples.ipynb: the six samples of examples.py pasted into notebook cells; deduplicated to the .py, which exercises every code path the notebook holds
